title: Drug use disorders and substance-induced psychosis
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's substance use disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for maintenance therapy.

HPI: The patient is an 86-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up regarding his treatment for opioid use disorder. He is currently managed on a buprenorphine maintenance regimen. He reports that he is in early remission and has maintained sobriety for 5 months. He reports stable mood and denies any cravings or difficulties with adherence to his current medication. He states he feels well and is satisfied with his current progress.

Medication List:
- Buprenorphine: 16mg daily
- Multivitamin: 1 daily

Vitals:
BP: 132/84
HR: 72 bpm
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on room air
Weight: 175 lbs

Recent Labs:
HbA1c: 6.2%
eGFR: 68 mL/min/1.73m2
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L

Review of Systems:
General: Denies fever, chills, or fatigue.
HEENT: Denies vision changes or headaches.
Respiratory: Denies shortness of breath or cough.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or palpitations.
Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain or nausea.
Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain or stiffness.
Neurological: Denies tremors or dizziness.
Psychiatric: Denies anxiety or sleep disturbances.

Social History: The patient lives in a private residence with his spouse. He enjoys gardening and watching television. He does not currently work.

Family History: Father had hypertension; mother had type 2 diabetes.

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Well-groomed and in no acute distress.
Psychiatric: Cooperative and pleasant. Speech is clear and coherent. Affect is congruent with mood.
Neurological: Normal gait and steady balance. No tremors noted.
Skin: Intact, no rashes or lesions.

Assessment:
1. Opioid use disorder, severe. The patient is currently in early remission. He has successfully avoided any illicit use for 5 months while on buprenorphine.

Plan:
1. Continue buprenorphine maintenance at the current dose.
2. Continue to monitor for stability and adherence.
3. Follow up in 3 months for continued evaluation of remission status.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Severe opioid use disorder in early remission: opioid dependence, in remission, F11.21 (HCC 137).

hccs.label: Drug Use Disorder/Moderate/Severe/Drug Use with Non-Psychotic Complications
